title: Microsoft Purview: delete inactive OneDrives and mailboxes for departed users (Worldwide)
summary: The roadmap facts and documented background controls check out, and the briefing keeps the planned capability separate from existing priority cleanup. Narrow the suggestion that the new capability deletes held data, clarify the abbreviated policy-creation route, and remove a checklist instruction without a corresponding control row.

claims.claim: Unexpired retention on items in a user's Preservation Hold library prevents deleting that OneDrive site.
claims.quote: When one or more items in a Preservation Hold library have an unexpired retention period, the OneDrive site for the user can't be deleted.

claims.claim: An inactive mailbox can be permanently deleted by removing all holds.
claims.quote: you can permanently delete the mailbox by removing all holds on it.

claims.claim: Deletion by the new capability removes data that may be under retention or eDiscovery hold.
claims.quote: Searched: "delete" "containers" "departed" Purview OneDrive mailbox; Purview delete inactive OneDrives mailboxes departed users containers 566527 default licensing. Read roadmap and priority cleanup pages; only existing priority cleanup is documented as overriding holds.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Managing SharePoint and OneDrive priority cleanup and enabling or disabling it requires Priority Cleanup Admin.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, this role is required to create and manage priority cleanup policies, and enable or disable the feature.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive priority cleanup requires another person's approval besides the policy creator.
claims.quote: each item subject to priority cleanup always requires at least one other person to approve the deletion in addition to the person who created the priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive priority cleanup policies require at least one simulation run before activation.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, you must run simulation at least one time, and for any change other than the policy description.

claims.claim: Auditing must be enabled at least one day before the first priority cleanup policy is created and run.
claims.quote: Make sure that auditing is enabled at least one day before you create and run the first priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: After removal of the final hold, an inactive mailbox is permanently deleted after the 30-day soft-deleted retention period.
claims.quote: if you remove the final hold from an inactive mailbox the mailbox will be permanently deleted after the 30-day soft-deleted mailbox retention period expires. After the inactive mailbox is permanently deleted, it can't be recovered.

claims.claim: The tenant priority cleanup control is at Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration > control for priority cleanup in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management.
From the top right, select Priority cleanup settings.
From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup, and select Save.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for the tenant priority cleanup enable/disable control.
claims.quote: Searched: priority cleanup tenant configuration disable PowerShell Set Graph API; "priority cleanup" "Set-PolicyConfig". Opened both priority cleanup pages and New-RetentionCompliancePolicy; results document portal configuration, not a tenant enable/disable call.

claims.claim: Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup opens creation of a OneDrive priority cleanup policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup, and then select + Create a priority cleanup.
claims.fix: Clarify that the printed route opens the wizard. For a static OneDrive policy, the documented continuation is Choose the type of priority cleanup > Static > Policy for SharePoint/OneDrive > Tell us what you're looking for > Choose when content should be deleted > Assign who'll approve what gets deleted > Choose the policy mode. State in the existing note that the OneDrive location, query and approvers are configured in the wizard and that the initial policy runs in simulation. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/priority-cleanup-onedrive-sharepoint#create-a-priority-cleanup-policy.

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -PriorityCleanup creates a Priority cleanup policy in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote:
The PriorityCleanup switch specifies whether to create a Priority cleanup policy. You don't need to specify a value with this switch.
The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the retention policy.

claims.claim: Set-Mailbox <identity of inactive mailbox> -ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds removes an inactive mailbox from whole-location retention policies using older locations in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Static scope: How to remove an inactive mailbox from a retention policy that's configured for the entire location
For retention policies that use the older retention locations
Set-Mailbox <identity of inactive mailbox> -ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds

claims.claim: The documented inactive mailbox hold-removal procedures use PowerShell, not the Exchange admin center or Purview portal.
claims.quote: You must use Exchange Online PowerShell to remove holds from an inactive mailbox. You can't use the Exchange admin center (EAC), or the Microsoft Purview portal for these procedures.

claims.claim: An inactive mailbox cannot be removed from a retention policy with Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: You won't be able to remove an inactive mailbox if the retention policy has Preservation Lock applied.

claims.claim: Select Audit and then Start recording user and admin activity in the Microsoft Purview portal to enable auditing.
claims.quote:
Select the Audit solution card.
If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity.
Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true enables organisation auditing using Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.
Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell.
Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true
